uncited: Ray Traversal Algorithms are a family of hierarchical descent methods used to efficiently determine which nodes of a sparse voxel octree (SVO) or similar tree structure intersect a given ray.
They solve the problem of avoiding redundant intersection tests in large, sparse volumetric datasets by skipping empty subtrees and jumping directly to occupied leaf nodes or boundary cells.

This family is distinguished from sibling methods like [GPU Octree Volume Rasterization](5209-gpu-octree-volume-rasterization-with-shadow-mapping.md) by its reliance on explicit ray-tree intersection logic rather than rasterization primitives, and from [Camera-Driven Octree Subdivision](7636-camera-driven-octree-subdivision.md) by its focus on per-ray traversal state rather than global view-dependent subdivision.
The traversal begins at the root of the octree and determines which of the eight children (octants) the ray intersects.
The implementation does not use SIMD or packet tracing.
